messages:
sam: Heads-up — customer acme-inc seeing a burst of 502/504s hitting Hosted API during a large embeddings + billing-sync job, started ~2026-03-17T09:12Z. They report >100 errors in 10m window and errors surface as gateway 502 / upstream timeouts 504.

lina: Can you paste a few trace ids and an example request (sanitized)?

sam: Trace IDs: t-67a1, t-67a4, t-67b0. Example error shows Envoy returning 502 with upstream reset and nginx reporting downstream write timeout.

ops_jordan: Pulling logs now — grabbing envoy access + upstream proxy for the tenant. Looks like a lot of long-lived h2 streams hitting keepalive pool limits and slow_write on billing backend.

sam: Customer repro steps (what they ran):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --http2 \
  --data '{"model":"embed-xl","inputs":[...large batch...]}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings
```
They stream lots of tokens and concurrently run a billing write endpoint call that spikes the billing proxy.

marco: Quick observations from envoy logs: upstream reset_before_response_started, stream_idle_timeout for some streams, and many connections hit backend slow_write with EAGAIN. This is classic keepalive + upstream slow consumer interaction causing connection window stalls --> envoy returns 502 / 504.

natalie: Any recent deploys to hosted edge or billing proxy? Could be a regression in the billing service's socket handling.

deploy-bot: canary-deploy/billing-proxy v3.4.2 -> v3.5.0 started at 2026-03-17T08:50Z. 20% traffic.

ops_jordan: Aha — canary overlapped with the customer workload window. v3.5.0 has a change to socket write buffering (smaller write buffer + different epoll flags). Rolling back canary to confirm.

marco: Immediate mitigation options:
- Rollback billing-proxy v3.5.0 from canary (if confirmed).
- Temporary route-level concurrency cap for heavy embed tenant (cap concurrent requests: 8).
- Increase envoy upstream connection pool and keepalive settings for billing cluster to avoid starving new streams.
- Tune upstream socket write buffer or enable burst queueing on billing worker.

sam: Trying rollback now. Also documented curl to reproduce so devs can test locally.

deploy-bot: canary-deploy/billing-proxy rollback initiated at 2026-03-17T09:23:11Z by ops_jordan.

lina: While rollback is running, can we add a temporary rule to abort long streaming requests after 60s and return 429 to the tenant? That would limit cascade.

marco: Yes — we can add a route-level timeout and a small early-fail policy to avoid filling upstream queues. I'll send the change.

ops_jordan: Rollback complete. Early telemetry: error rate for tenant down from ~12% -> 1.5% in the last 3m. Still seeing a few stragglers from slow clients.

sam: Customer notified of mitigation and asked to retry after 5m. They ran the same curl after rollback and got 200 for three consecutive attempts.

natalie: Postmortem actions (tentative):
- Revert or patch billing-proxy v3.5.0 to respect larger write buffers for high-concurrency tenants.
- Add automated canary health checks that include high-concurrency streaming scenarios.
- Add route-level concurrency & early-fail for heavy batch embed endpoints.
- Update runbook: when seeing upstream slow_write + keepalive exhaustion, consider canary rollback and temporary concurrency cap before scaling.

sam: Thanks team. I'll follow up with a short summary to customer and create a ticket for the billing-proxy patch. :thumbsup:

lina: Thanks — capturing traces + logs in the support ticket (see trace ids above).

ops_jordan: Leaving a note: if you need quick repro, use --http2 + a 50kB body and a billing write triggered concurrently, should repro on dev when proxy is on v3.5.0.

marco: Closing this thread once postmortem ticket is created.

sam: Closing after I file the PM ticket.
